idea:
Shot 1: wide shot of a rain-soaked train platform at night, an old station clock above shows 11:58; a young woman in a yellow raincoat with short silver hair runs toward the last train.
  Shot 2: inside the empty carriage a tired conductor in his sixties with a grey moustache blocks the door and says: "Ticket's $4.50, and this train left Kyiv in 1987 — it doesn't stop for
  anyone." Shot 3: she holds up a faded paper ticket and answers: "I bought this one thirty-eight years ago. You promised you'd wait."

script.title: The Kyiv Express
script.logline: On a rainy midnight platform, a young woman chases a ghostly train that departed decades ago to claim a long-promised reunion.
script.setting: rain-soaked Kyiv train station platform and vintage passenger carriage at night

characters.name: Olena
characters.look: 24-year-old woman, short silver hair, soaked pale skin, oversized bright yellow raincoat, dark jeans, muddy combat boots
characters.voiceDescription: breathless urgent female voice, mid-20s, slight Eastern European accent, trembling pace

characters.name: Bohdan
characters.look: 65-year-old man, thick grey moustache, deep facial wrinkles, dark navy Soviet-era railway uniform coat, brass buttons, peaked conductor cap
characters.voiceDescription: raspy low male voice, mid-60s, Eastern European accent, weary and deadpan

shots.visual: On a dimly lit rain-swept concrete platform beneath an ornate station clock reading 11:58, Olena in her bright yellow raincoat sprints desperately toward the glowing doors of a vintage passenger carriage.
shots.motion: slow pull-back tracking her forward sprint

shots.visual: Inside the narrow threshold of the train carriage, Bohdan in his navy coat and peaked cap stands firm, blocking the open doorway as wind and mist blow past him.
shots.line:
Ticket's $4.50, and this train left Kyiv in 1987 — it doesn't stop for
  anyone.
shots.speaker: Bohdan

cuts.visual: Inside the narrow threshold of the train carriage, Bohdan in his navy coat and peaked cap stands firm, blocking the open doorway as wind and mist blow past him.
Bohdan's tired wrinkled face hardened under his peaked cap as his grey moustache twitches with a cold, unyielding glare.
Olena's soaked face freezing on the threshold, rain dripping from her silver bangs as she catches her breath in disbelief.

shots.visual: Olena raises a trembling hand into frame, clutching a faded, water-damaged paper ticket directly before Bohdan with desperate hope in her eyes.
shots.line: I bought this one thirty-eight years ago. You promised you'd wait.
shots.speaker: Olena

cuts.visual: Olena raises a trembling hand into frame, clutching a faded, water-damaged paper ticket directly before Bohdan with desperate hope in her eyes.
Bohdan's guarded expression falters, his weathered eyes widening slightly in sudden, haunting recognition.
Olena steps onto the carriage bottom step in the pouring rain, holding Bohdan's stunned gaze under the doorway lamp.
